claim_verdicts.evidence: observer-design-pattern.md: "Observers register with the provider, and whenever a predefined condition, event, or state change occurs, the provider automatically notifies all observers by calling a delegate." + "it supports a clean separation between two different components". Matches subscribe / provider keeps list / calls each; lesson code (OrderEvents names neither subscriber) shows the 'without knowing what they do' part.

keywords/event.md: "The `event` keyword declares an event. The event is of a delegate type." / "Events are multicast delegates that you can only invoke from within the class ... where you declare them (the publisher class)." how-to-subscribe...md: "Use the addition assignment operator (`+=`) to attach an event handler to the event." Code at stage-2 line 9: `public event Action<int>? OrderPlaced;`.

events/index.md: "When an event has multiple subscribers, the event handlers are invoked synchronously when an event is raised." using-delegates.md: "When allMethodsDelegate is invoked, all three methods are called in order." using-delegates.md: "When any of the methods throws an exception that isn't caught within the method, that exception is passed to the caller of the delegate. No subsequent methods in the invocation list are called." Run at stage-2: AThrowingHandlerStopsTheRestAndReachesPlace passes (Assert.Throws + Assert.Empty(log)).

event-pattern.md: "you also must declare a private backing field to store the event variable. This variable is initialized to null." delegates-patterns.md: "will throw a NullReferenceException when the WriteMessage delegate does not have an invocation list attached" ... "The null conditional operator (?.) short-circuits when the left operand ... is null" with `WriteMessage?.Invoke(msg);`.

delegates-lambdas.md: "System.Action`1 (and Action<T1, T2>, and so on) represents a method that returns nothing (void). All type parameters are input types." covariance-and-contravariance.md: a lambda "that takes one parameter ... and that has no return value" assigned to Action<Derived>.
